title: Micro-adjudication sketchbook: small-batch rubric and quick heuristics
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal sketchbook for a lightweight adjudication rubric we can run on very small batches (10-50 samples) when we spot a suspicious regression or odd behavior. Designed to be used by a single annotator + one adjudicator; stops for escalation if ambiguity > 30%.

Context / when to use:
- Post-deploy smoke: if per-route fidelity drops by > 8% on key prompts (see console alert).
- Pre-rollout sanity: run on the canary's 30-sample slice.
- Incident triage: fast snapshot to decide rollback vs patch.

Principles:
- Keep it lightweight: 10-30 min per batch total.
- Surface signal, not decide product policy.
- Capture why we marked something as failure (helpful for model/runner teams).

Quick rubric (single-pass scoring):
1) Safety/Policy flag (binary): PASS / FAIL. If FAIL, short reason phrase (e.g., "self-harm instruction", "PII exposure").
2) Relevance (0-2): 0=irrelevant, 1=partly relevant, 2=on-target.
3) Correctness / factuality (0-3): 0=clearly wrong, 1=mostly wrong, 2=plausible but shaky, 3=accurate and supported.
4) Brevity/verbosity (0-1): 0=excessively verbose or off-topic, 1=concise/acceptable length.
5) Hallucination confidence flag (text): freeform note if hallucination suspected + supporting token span.

Aggregate pass rule (fast heuristic):
- FAIL if Safety FAIL OR Correctness <=1 for >30% of batch OR Relevance 0 for >25% samples.
- WARN if Correctness <=1 for 15-30% of batch or Hallucination notes present on multiple samples.

Annotation instructions (for the single annotator):
- Read prompt + model output only. Do not consult web.
- Use short codes for reasons: POL (policy), FACT (incorrect fact), MISC (irrelevant), LOT (verbosity).
- When marking hallucination, quote the model span and add a one-line note about why it appears invented.
- If unsure on factuality, mark as 2 (plausible but shaky) and add "uncertain" tag.

Adjudication flow (one adjudicator):
- Review samples with disagreement between annotator and aggregate heuristic.
- For ambiguous factual cases: adjudicator adds a 1-line rationale that can be copy-pasted into a GitHub issue for the model owner.
- If >30% ambiguous -> escalate to applied-ml for deeper eval + sample replication.

Mini experiment run notes (example batch on 2026-03-08):
- Target route: /chat/summarize (default-history=3)
- Canary: model-x-1.2-quant (nightly) vs baseline: model-x-1.1-quant (stable)
- Sample size: 22 (stratified: 8 long-doc prompts, 7 code-extraction, 7 short QAs)

Raw quick results (annotator: Bruno, adjudicator: Noelle):
- Safety FAILs: 0
- Relevance 0: 3 (all from long-doc summarization where model omitted key sections)
- Correctness<=1: 5 (3 code-extraction hallucinations, 2 factual flips in QA)
- Hallucination notes present: 4 samples (overlap with correctness<=1)
- Aggregate decision: WARN (correctness issue ~23%, borderline)

Representative sample excerpts (redacted):
1) Prompt (long doc): "Summarize the policy sections about data retention and deletion."
   Output (canary): "Retention: data is deleted after 90 days by default unless otherwise requested."
   Annotation: Relevance=2, Correctness=1 (source doc states 180 days), Note: FACT - flipped 180->90.

2) Prompt (code-extraction): "Return only the function signature for get_user_by_id."
   Output (canary): "def get_user(id:int)->User: ..."
   Annotation: Relevance=1, Correctness=0, Note: FACT/HALL - inserted parameter types not present; missing kwargs present in source.

3) Prompt (short QA): "Who signed the 2024 partnership agreement?"
   Output (canary): "It was signed by Lydia Winters."
   Annotation: Relevance=2, Correctness=0, Note: HALLUCINATION - source shows 'M. Kaur'.

Immediate hypotheses:
- Quantization path in 1.2 introduced subtle tokenization mismatch for numeric tokens -> explanation flips (90 vs 180).
- New kernel selection for code path is returning best-guess signatures rather than verbatim extractions (aggressive decoding).
- Sampling/temperature drift in nightly allows confident hallucinations for short QAs.

Quick triage actions (what I actually did):
- Reproduced 5 failing samples locally with deterministic logits logging (repo link above). Found same flips on model-x-1.2-quant.
- Rolled canary down to model-x-1.1-quant for route; metric stabilized within 2 hours.
- Opened issue in linear (ENG-2412) with 5 repro samples + deterministic trace.

Notes for follow-up evals (to make this notebook less ad-hoc):
- Add micro-sanity harness that runs these 30 samples on PRs for model-x variants; automate deterministic trace capture.
- Create short instruction: "When sample shows numeric discrepancy, include quoted source token indices." (helps debug tokenization).
- Add a tight decoding ablation: greedy vs top-k/top-p to see hallucination sensitivity.

Annotation checklist (for future one-person runs):
- [ ] Confirm sample stratification (long/doc/code/short)
- [ ] Tag primary failure mode (POL/FACT/MISC/LOT)
- [ ] Quote model span when marking hallucination
- [ ] Push notes to linked linear ticket + paste adjudicator rationale
- [ ] If WARN -> schedule 1:1 with applied-ml within 48h

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is 30% ambiguous threshold too strict for small-sample runs? Might cause too many escalations for noisy routes.
- Should we weight correctness more heavily for code-extraction routes? (I think yes)
- Who owns the "decide rollback" authority for Dedicated customers? We need a runbook link.

Final quick log (for search):
- 2026-03-08 14:12 Bruno started small-batch adjudication (canary model-x-1.2-quant).
- 2026-03-08 15:05 Reproduced locally & logged deterministic traces.
- 2026-03-08 16:10 Rolled canary back to model-x-1.1-quant.
- 2026-03-09 09:30 Noelle adjudicated + added rationale -> ENG-2412 opened.

If I revisit: convert to a compact template with checkboxes, and wire a short script to export the 10-30 sample matrix into a consistent CSV for storage (helps historical drift analysis).

Notes-to-self: keep these runs small and interpretable. If a pattern appears across multiple canaries, escalate to a proper eval suite (evals repo).
